tier1_policy: Tier 1 requests are sent only on a scan that asks for active probes, at most once per target domain every 6 hours, and never to a domain whose verified owner turned active probes off.

rows.title: Document exists
rows.pass_when: https://{domain}/.well-known/poppy.json (or its www or apex sibling, see T0-SIB) answers 2xx, after at most 5 redirects, with a JSON object naming protocol_version or organization. A body sent as JSON that does not parse, is not an object or is over 100 KB also counts as found (and fails T0-03); a JSON object with neither key, an HTML page or any other body reads as no file

rows.title: Redirects safe
rows.pass_when: Every redirect hop on the way to poppy.json is HTTPS, and the last URL's path is exactly /.well-known/poppy.json, with no query

rows.title: Valid JSON object
rows.pass_when: The body parses as a JSON object of at most 100 KB

rows.title: Version a 1.0 agent can use
rows.pass_when: protocol_version is "1.0" or a later 1.x minor, which is compatible with 1.0 (spec 3.4); every file is graded by the 1.0 rules. A file that declares a 0.x draft fails, since no 1.0 agent uses it, and the failure stops no other check. It passes when supported_versions links a 1.0 document by https on the host that served poppy.json, and the other rows still grade poppy.json, not the linked document. A missing protocol_version, one that is not a string, or one not written as major.minor without leading or trailing zeros fails and stops the other checks. A later major reads not tested, and the rest of the file is graded as 1.0

rows.title: Organization names its own host
rows.pass_when: organization has a name and a domain, and organization.domain is the host that served the file after any redirects, compared ignoring case only (a leading www. counts), and it carries that host's port when the port is not 443 (spec 3.1)

rows.title: Has an interface
rows.pass_when: The file has at least one interface: an agent object, a non-empty apis array or a web object, and web.disabled needs agent or apis too

rows.title: Issuer identified

request.condition: when the file is served by the host its organization.domain names

rows.pass_when: The issuer comes from the protected resource metadata of https://{organization.domain}, following redirects only within that domain. A 404, or metadata whose resource is that URL and which lists no authorization server, means no issuer, which passes unless auth.issuer, signed_in access or Mediated Sign-In needs one; one server is the issuer (auth.issuer, when set, names it); several need auth.issuer to name one of them. Any other answer fails, a rate limit or server error included, since an agent never falls back to the domain; a bot challenge reads blocked and metadata past Ora's 100 KB read cap reads not tested

rows.title: All URLs HTTPS
rows.pass_when: Every URL field the spec defines, and every string in the file that carries a URL scheme, is an absolute https URL. An optional block that carries a URL (tasks) and is an object without it gets an advisory note, since spec 3.1 states no MUST that it carry one; a URL that is there must be https, and a block value that is not an object fails. Every supported_versions URL is on the host that served poppy.json

rows.title: Published on the requested host

request.condition: when the requested host has no file and its homepage resolved to the sibling

rows.pass_when: Ora's lookup, not defined by the spec: poppy.json is served on the requested host itself, not only on its www or apex sibling

rows.title: Other version documents consistent

request.condition: when the file lists one on the host that served it; up to 3, no redirect followed

rows.pass_when: Each document supported_versions links to answers 200 with no redirect, since an agent must not follow one; declares the protocol_version it is listed under; has no supported_versions of its own; and names the same organization.domain and selects the same issuer as poppy.json, so a new version does not change the Company's identifier. Ora reads at most 3, each on the host that served poppy.json (T0-08 grades entries on another host). Blocked when a bot shield answers; not tested when a document is past Ora's 100 KB read cap or the Company's issuer is not known; N/A without supported_versions, or when poppy.json fails a row an agent stops at (T0-02, T0-05, T0-06, T0-07, or T0-04 for a missing or malformed protocol_version)

rows.title: Issuer metadata reachable

request.condition: when the domain's protected resource metadata names the issuer (T0-07)

rows.pass_when: The issuer's RFC 8414 metadata (/.well-known/oauth-authorization-server for the issuer, following redirects only within the issuer's registrable domain) answers 200 with a JSON object. An issuer whose host resolves to a loopback, private, link-local or other non-public address fails (spec 3), since no agent may connect to it

rows.title: Issuer match
rows.pass_when: The metadata's issuer is exactly the issuer T0-07 found

rows.title: Domain binding
rows.pass_when: The metadata's protected_resources lists https://{organization.domain}, host case aside, with no path or trailing slash (the domain, and so the entry, carries its port when that is not 443, spec 3.1)

rows.title: Issuer metadata URLs well formed
rows.pass_when: Every entry of the issuer metadata's protected_resources is an https URL (spec 3) with no fragment (RFC 9728 section 1.2). The issuer MAY list resources other than its domains (spec 3.2), and Ora cannot tell one with no path from a domain written another way, so an entry with no path that has a trailing slash, a query or the default port 443 is an advisory note (if it is one of the issuer's domains, list it as https://{domain}) and never fails the check. Entries on the scanned domain's host are T0-11's, and the metadata's issuer is T0-10's. N/A without protected_resources (T0-11 fails)

rows.title: Required endpoints
rows.pass_when: The metadata has https token_endpoint and revocation_endpoint, a grant_types_supported that includes refresh_token, plus authorization_endpoint when that list has authorization_code and device_authorization_endpoint when it has the device_code grant

rows.title: Pushed authorization requests usable
rows.pass_when: A pushed_authorization_request_endpoint the issuer metadata lists is an https URL (spec 3), and when grant_types_supported has authorization_code, require_pushed_authorization_requests set to true comes with that endpoint, since an agent must then push its Direct Sign-In request there (spec 4.2, RFC 9126 section 5). Each gap warns and never fails the check (P2, product owner decision): requiring Pushed Authorization Requests is a choice the Company may make, and a non-https endpoint breaks spec 3 only for agents that push. N/A when the metadata neither lists the endpoint nor requires them, or when it requires them but offers no Direct Sign-In

rows.title: Signing algorithms valid
rows.pass_when: When the issuer metadata lists token_endpoint_auth_signing_alg_values_supported (it may leave it out), the list includes ES256 and PS384, which every Company accepts for client assertions (spec 4.1), and never none (T0-34 grades the list's absence next to a JWT method). N/A when the list is not given

rows.title: Signing algorithm list advertised
rows.pass_when: When token_endpoint_auth_methods_supported lists private_key_jwt or client_secret_jwt, the issuer metadata also lists token_endpoint_auth_signing_alg_values_supported, as RFC 8414 section 2 requires. Every Company accepts ES256 and PS384 client assertions (spec 4.1), so the list only restates that rule, and Ora grades the gap as a warning, never failing the check. N/A when neither method is listed

rows.title: Same sign-in on every domain

request.target: each other domain the issuer binds (its protected_resources): /.well-known/poppy.json, and /.well-known/oauth-protected-resource when that file names no auth.issuer
request.condition: when the issuer binding holds and the issuer lists other domains, at most 3

rows.pass_when: Every other domain in the issuer's protected_resources (the first 3) selects the same issuer (with an advisory when it describes a scope both files list differently, spec 3.2 SHOULD), and every such domain that lists a browser_session_endpoint sets web.unscoped the same way. A domain whose poppy.json names no auth.issuer selects its issuer through its own protected resource metadata, which Ora reads as it reads the scanned domain's (T0-07): a domain that selects none is not compared, and one whose metadata Ora could not read or use reads not tested. N/A when protected_resources lists no other domain

rows.title: No plain PKCE
rows.pass_when: code_challenge_methods_supported, when the metadata lists it, does not include plain

rows.title: Scopes defined
rows.pass_when: Each Company defines its own scopes: every auth.scopes entry has a description, every auth.scope_hints entry has a changes value and a boolean personal_data, and web.unscoped comes with a browser_session_endpoint (N/A when none of these is set)

rows.title: Mediated sign-in well formed
rows.pass_when: The Mediated Sign-In extension's version 1 entry has a non-empty fields list (each with a label, a boolean secret and a name that is no OAuth or extension parameter) and scopes, and the issuer's grant_types_supported lists its grant when the metadata was read (T0-24 grades it next to auth.disabled)

rows.title: Extensions named correctly
rows.pass_when: Every extension name is one the protocol defines (operations, mediated-sign-in, links, disclosures, ucp and browser-control) or is prefixed with a domain (example.com/name), and every extension is a list of entries that each carry a version

rows.title: Extensions advertised fully
rows.pass_when: extensions.operations has a version "3" entry (with no entry at that version, agents ignore it and the row reads N/A); an operations entry with an endpoint has an https one, and an operations endpoint comes with web.browser_session_endpoint (a browser-control entry without one is an advisory note)

rows.title: Switched off consistently
rows.pass_when: auth.disabled, when set, is true or false, and a file that sets it to true lists neither the Mediated Sign-In extension nor a conversation entry with access set to signed_in; web.disabled set to true comes with no browser_session_endpoint. N/A when neither is set

rows.title: Offered scopes described
rows.pass_when: Every scope in the issuer's scopes_supported and in the scopes_supported of the domain's protected resource metadata, which agents read with it, has a description, in auth.scopes or in the OAuth flows of a listed OpenAPI document, so an agent can ask for only what a task needs; a scope agents cannot request can be left out of those lists. The spec says SHOULD; Ora weighs it for user experience, so a gap warns and never fails the check. OpenID Connect's standard scopes (openid, profile, email, address, phone, offline_access) are skipped. Not tested when a scope is still undescribed and a listed OpenAPI document could not be read, or the file lists the UCP extension, whose profile may hold the description; N/A when there is no issuer or the lists name no other scope

rows.title: Browser sign-in scope listed
rows.pass_when: When the file lists web.browser_session_endpoint and the Company offers sign-in, poppy:browser-sign-in is in the issuer's scopes_supported or the scopes_supported of the domain's protected resource metadata (section 3.2 allows either or both, and agents read them as one list). The Company must support that scope (section 6) and should list every scope an agent can request (section 3.2), so a missing entry warns and never fails the check. Not tested when neither metadata document has scopes_supported (T0-35 warns about that); N/A without a browser join, with auth.disabled set to true, or with no issuer

rows.title: Requestable scopes listed
rows.pass_when: A Company that offers sign-in (its issuer's grant_types_supported lists authorization_code or the device grant, or the file lists Mediated Sign-In) lists the scopes an agent can request in scopes_supported, in the issuer's metadata, the domain's protected resource metadata, or both (spec 3.2, 4.7). The spec says SHOULD, so a missing list warns and never fails the check. Not tested when the issuer's metadata was not read; N/A with no issuer, with auth.disabled set to true, or when the Company offers no sign-in

rows.title: Conversation entries
rows.pass_when: agent.protocols is a non-empty list, each entry with a type and an https endpoint. Each entry also has a description of what the agent at that endpoint can help with (spec 8.1)

rows.title: API entries
rows.pass_when: apis is a non-empty list, each entry with a type (any type, not only openapi or mcp), an https url and a description

rows.title: OpenAPI parses

request.condition: when the file lists OpenAPI documents, at most 3

rows.pass_when: Each listed OpenAPI document (the first 3) is OpenAPI 3.0 or 3.1

rows.title: MCP resource metadata

request.condition: when the file lists MCP servers, at most 3, each with at most two GETs

rows.pass_when: The RFC 9728 protected resource metadata at each listed MCP server's own well-known URL (the first 3), or when that URL has none the resource_metadata URL a 401 from the server named to the scan's MCP discovery, names the server's url as its resource, and lists the issuer in authorization_servers when it lists any; a server whose metadata URL answers 404 offers no account access and is not counted

rows.title: Tasks endpoint usable
rows.pass_when: tasks.endpoint is on a host that is not a loopback, private or link-local IP address (spec 3); a missing endpoint is an advisory on T0-08 and a non-https one fails T0-08, so either reads N/A here. Ora does not request it: spec 9 lets a Company that gives every Session the same response serve it without checking the Session header, so a request without one proves nothing. N/A without a tasks block or without an https endpoint (see T0-08)

rows.title: UCP entry lists the UCP extension
rows.pass_when: A file whose agent.protocols lists a ucp entry also lists the UCP extension with a version "1" entry (UCP extension 5; an entry at another version is ignored by agents, so it fails too)

rows.title: UCP profile offers Ask

request.target: each ucp entry's endpoint, its UCP profile
request.condition: when the file lists a ucp agent entry on the host that served it; up to 2, no redirect followed

rows.pass_when: Each ucp entry names a UCP profile on the host that served poppy.json, which answers 200 with no redirect and JSON whose capabilities offer dev.ucp.common.ask with at least one version entry (UCP extension 3 and 5: an agent must not follow a redirect from the profile URL or use a profile from another host, so either fails; Ask is in UCP's current draft, so a profile that predates it fails)

rows.title: Same MCP server everywhere
rows.pass_when: Ora consistency check, not a spec requirement: every MCP server poppy.json lists has a server card in the site's ARD catalog

rows.title: Same organization
rows.pass_when: Ora consistency check, not a spec requirement: the site's ARD catalog host names the same organization as poppy.json (display name, and the did:web domain)

rows.title: Domains covered

request.target: each other domain the issuer binds (its protected_resources): /.well-known/poppy.json, and /.well-known/oauth-protected-resource when that file names no auth.issuer
request.condition: when the issuer binding holds and the issuer lists other domains, at most 3

rows.pass_when: Ora consistency check, not a spec requirement: each other domain the issuer binds (the first 3) serves a poppy.json naming the same issuer, or naming none; a www. host counts as its own domain

rows.title: Shared token endpoint lists both protocols' grants
rows.pass_when: Ora consistency check, not a spec requirement: where the PAP issuer also serves auth.md's agent_auth, grant_types_supported lists every grant both protocols send to its token endpoint (PAP's are refresh_token, and Mediated Sign-In's grant when listed)

rows.title: Consistent 401s
rows.pass_when: Ora consistency check, not a spec requirement: a recorded 401 challenge from a PAP MCP server points at the same resource metadata as T0-18

rows.title: Token endpoint rejects a junk grant

request.target: the token endpoint in the issuer's metadata
request.condition: when the Company has an issuer whose metadata has a token endpoint on the scanned domain; a token endpoint on another domain is not probed

rows.pass_when: Answers invalid_grant, invalid_client or unauthorized_client, or a DPoP proof error; a 403 extension_required reads not tested. Ora also passes invalid_request at any 4xx status, with an advisory note

rows.title: Error bodies leak nothing
rows.pass_when: No error body a probe got back carries a stack trace

rows.title: Conversation endpoint refuses a request with no credentials

request.target: {endpoint}/ora_probe/events on one conversation endpoint that poppy.json lists for the poppy protocol (an entry without access signed_in first, then the first in alphabetical order)

rows.pass_when: Answers 400 with invalid_session in a JSON body (a 400 version_unsupported reads not tested, since Poppy-Version may be checked first, and so does a 403 extension_required; a 401 asking for an account at an entry with access signed_in reads not tested, since that entry needs account access first and the spec does not order the two checks); a conversation_not_found answer fails, since the endpoint looked the conversation up without a Session header

rows.title: MCP server challenges unauthenticated initialize

request.target: one MCP server that poppy.json lists (the first in alphabetical order)

rows.pass_when: Answers 401 with resource_metadata on every Bearer or DPoP challenge. A server that completes initialize with no token, refuses it before any token check with 400 invalid_session, 400 version_unsupported or 403 extension_required in a JSON body, or rejects it with the 400 and MCP error of a server that speaks only MCP 2026-07-28 has no 401 challenge to grade, so the row reads not tested

rows.title: Browser join page is safe to load
rows.pass_when: Answers 200 with a form holding a code, a cookie that ties the code to the browser (SameSite Strict or Lax, and a __Host- name, since spec 6 says other hosts on the domain must not be able to set the cookie and only that prefix ensures it), Cache-Control: no-store, frame-ancestors 'none' (or X-Frame-Options: DENY) and a Cross-Origin-Opener-Policy that severs the opener

rows.title: Browser endpoint rejects a junk join
rows.pass_when: Answers an error status and no cookie (a CDN or load balancer cookie, or one the response clears, does not count)

rows.title: Browser join authorization requires a Session
rows.pass_when: Answers 400 invalid_session (a 400 invalid_request, a 403 extension_required or a 400 version_unsupported reads not tested)

rows.title: Website operations endpoint requires a Session

request.target: the endpoint of the operations extension's version 3 entry in poppy.json
request.condition: when the file lists one, as the last probe of the round, so it is sent only when the round has room under its cap of 6 requests

rows.pass_when: Answers 400 invalid_session (a 400 invalid_request, which a reference the Session cannot use also gets, a 400 version_unsupported or a 403 extension_required reads not tested)

rows.title: Protocol endpoints answer without a redirect
rows.pass_when: Every probed endpoint (token, conversation, MCP, the browser join's /authorize and the website operations endpoint; never the join page or form, whose success is a redirect) answers without a redirect, since an agent sends no token, Session header, DPoP proof, assertion or credentials to the URL a protocol endpoint redirects to

rows.title: Rate limits say when to retry
rows.pass_when: Every 429 a probe gets carries a Retry-After header, in seconds or as an HTTP date (spec 5.6). The probe that got the 429 still reads blocked; the spec states the header as what a Company sends, so a missing one warns and never fails the check. N/A when no probe got a 429
